messages:
eli.sales: Ping BlueCrest Labs wants a 6-day POC for our private deployment. Ask: single upload of ISO artifacts + full pen-test PDF, and they want evidence stored in our dataroom for reviewers in EU. Any residency or legal blockers?
sara.sec: EU residency matters. If they require EU-hosted storage, we must use their dedicated VPC region for the dataroom or confirm our EU region retention. Also need vendor-signed pen-test attestation that allows sharing with auditors.
mike.ops: We can provision a region-scoped presign path in eu-west-1 under `bluecrest/poc/`. Default lifecycle policy can be 21 days. Presign TTL should be 5 days to force quick upload. We'll enable access logging and MFA-delete for extra auditability.
rachel.legal: Important: vendor attestation must include explicit consent for Redwood to store reports in the EU, plus a liability disclaimer. I will add a clause: "Vendor consents to storage in EU region for 21 days and accepts that Redwood acts as custodian only."
eli.sales: Buyer also asked if Redwood can coordinate vendor signature and accept the ZIP on their behalf. They prefer us to do it due to timezones.
sara.sec: We can offer vendor-liaison but only after SOW signs; security needs the attestation to clearly state scope (staging subnets + container registries), retention (21 days), redaction window (5 days), and export controls (no public distribution). Snippet below: 

```
Pen-test attestation snippet:
- Scope: staging CIDRs and listed hostnames; container images included
- Retention: Redwood will retain raw reports in EU region for 21 days post-upload
- Redaction: Customer may request redaction within 5 days; Redwood will apply redaction and re-issue a redacted bundle within 48 hours
- Export/Sharing: Vendor confirms reports may be shared with customer-designated auditors; no public redistribution allowed
```

mike.ops: ops-bot generated presign token: https://eu-files.redwood.test/presign/bluecrest-poc?ttl=5d (sample). Generated at 1765001350. :white_check_mark:
eli.sales: Pricing implications: private EU dataroom + region-scoped storage = small uplift. Also vendor-liaison and redaction SOW are optional add-ons. I'll update the quote with: "EU dataroom handling (21d)", "Vendor liaison (optional)", "Redaction SOW (optional)".
rachel.legal: I'll add the EU consent clause and vendor-liaison terms to the attestation. Also add a clause restricting Redwood liability for vendor data content.
zoe.eng: Engineering note: if they want on-prem scanning to run against their staging, we'll need temporary networking rules. That requires their network whitelist and a maintenance window; propose Sat 00:00-03:00 CET for minimal interference.
sara.sec: Also check export control flags: some customers require that reports do not leave EU control plane. Confirmed: we'll keep data in EU region only.
eli.sales: Buyer requested ISO artifact list (cert cover, system description, control matrix). I'll attach a checklist to the quote.
mike.ops: Confirmed presign path, EU TTL and lifecycle. Will enable object-level audit and TLS-only endpoints. Final S3 URL will be DM'd once vendor signs.
rachel.legal: Draft attestation uploaded to the dataroom. Tagging @sara.sec for sign-off and then I'll send to vendor.
sara.sec: Reviewed and approved wording. Small edit: change redaction window from 5 -> 7 days? Buyer insisted on 5, so keep 5. Approved.
eli.sales: Great. Next steps: legal send to vendor, ops share final presign URL, sales send revised quote with EU dataroom uplift. If vendor needs us to sign anything extra, flag it here.
audit-bot: compliance-record: presign-created eu region, lifecycle=21d, ttl=5d, ticket=CR-4982. Generated at 1765001450.
eli.sales: Thanks all. Will post final presign URL and updated quote here after vendor signs. :pray:
